**Sikhae (시계) – Korean Traditional Rice Cake** Sikhae is a simple, comforting dish made from steamed rice flour (also called “sikhae” or “rice cake”) mixed with water and a pinch of salt. It’s often served as a side dish (banchan) or as a snack. Below is a straightforward recipe you can try at home. --- ### Ingredients | Ingredient | Amount | Notes | |------------|--------|-------| | Rice flour (short‑grain, Korean “sikhae” flour) | 1 cup (≈120 g) | If you can’t find Korean rice flour, use regular short‑grain rice flour. | | Water | 1 ½ cups (≈360 ml) | Adjust slightly for desired consistency. | | Salt | ¼ teaspoon | Optional, for flavor. | | Optional add‑ins | | • Sesame seeds (for garnish)
• Gochugaru (Korean red pepper flakes)
• Soy sauce or sesame oil (for dipping) | --- ### Equipment - Steamer or pot with a steaming rack - Mixing bowl - Whisk or spoon - Heat‑resistant container or mold (optional) --- ### Instructions #### 1. Prepare the Steamer Fill a pot with about 2 inches of water and bring it to a boil. Place a steaming rack or a heat‑resistant bowl inside. Make sure the water level is below the rack so the mixture won’t touch the water directly. #### 2. Mix the Dough In a mixing bowl, combine the rice flour and salt. Gradually pour in the water while whisking continuously to avoid lumps. The batter should be smooth and slightly thick—similar to a pancake batter but a bit more viscous. #### 3. Steam the Mixture Pour the batter into a heat‑resistant container or a shallow pan that fits inside the steamer. Cover the container with a lid or a clean kitchen towel. Steam for **15–20 minutes** until the mixture becomes translucent and firm to the touch. If you’re using a mold, press the batter gently into the shape before steaming. #### 4. Cool & Slice Remove the container from the steamer and let it cool for a few minutes. Once it’s safe to handle, cut the steamed cake into bite‑size squares or thin slices. If you prefer a softer texture, you can steam for a shorter time (about 12 minutes) and slice immediately. #### 5. Serve Place the sliced sikhae on a plate. Sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds or a pinch of gochugaru if you like a little spice. Serve with a small bowl of soy sauce or a drizzle of sesame oil for dipping. Sikhae pairs wonderfully with kimchi, pickled vegetables, or a light soup. --- ### Tips & Variations | Tip | Explanation | |-----|-------------| | **Texture** | For a chewier texture, steam longer (up to 25 min). For a softer, more delicate bite, steam shorter (around 12 min). | | **Flavor** | Add a splash of soy sauce or a drizzle of sesame oil to the batter before steaming for extra umami. | | **Presentation** | Mold the batter into a rectangular shape before steaming for a neat, uniform look. | | **Storage** | Store leftover sikhae in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat in the microwave or steam again briefly before serving. | Enjoy your homemade sikhae! It’s a quick, wholesome addition to any Korean meal.
